paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: coming back to the LORD is real, and it costs something. Samuel says, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the foreign gods and Ashtoreths among you, prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only" (1 Samuel 7:3). Israel did it, and they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD" (1 Samuel 7:6). Twenty years of mournful seeking ended with a people who stopped hanging on to what pulled them away and turned to Him with their whole hearts.

Now look at what happens when the Philistines march up. Israel is afraid, and they don't run and they don't make a plan of their own. They ask Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us" (1 Samuel 7:8). Then the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines, and the Philistines fled (1 Samuel 7:10). Israel didn't win because they were brave. They won because they cried out to the LORD, and He answered.

Then Samuel sets up a stone and says, "Thus far the LORD has helped us" (1 Samuel 7:12). I love that, baker. He doesn't say the LORD helped us once, he points back at the whole road. So here's your homework: put up your own Ebenezer. Remember where the LORD has helped you, and keep crying out to Him, because He still answers. And this isn't the end of Samuel's story, because there's more still to come.
